newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Nera shows improved second quarter.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nera shows improved second quarter.

text.p: Norwegian telecommunications company Nera ASA booked on Wednesday first half pre-tax profits at 66.4 million crowns, up 18 percent, or 10 million crowns from a year ago.
Six month operating profits increased six percent to 75.24 million crowns against 70.85 million crowns, and earnings per share rose to 0.76 crowns from 0.64 crowns per share.

Nera, Norway's largest manufacturer of wireless telecommunications equipment and systems, said that after a relatively weak first quarter, orders and sales improved during the second three-month period.

Order intake in the second quarter amounted to 955 million crowns, the highest ever recorded by the group in a single quarter, while sales between April and June jumped 42 percent from the corresponding year-ago period to 764 million crowns.

It added that healthy sales of the group's WorldPhone satellite phone and a 20 million crown profit, booked in first-half accounts, from the sale of the Risoer plant in southern Norway also contributed to the positive results.

In a statement, Frode Botnevik, Nera executive chairman, said the group saw growth in volumes of 10 to 15 percent as "realistic", although the competitive situation provided an element of uncertainty over Nera's operating margins.
"In the short term, cost reductions and continued restructuring of the company must go hand in hand with extensive product development and marketing," Botnevik said.

First half new orders for Nera's transmission network business fell to 696 million crowns versus 751 million crowns. Nera said new orders picked up in the second quarter to stand at 448 million crowns compared with 248 million crowns in Q296.

Nera President Ashbjoern Birkeland said increased competition had resulted in slimmer margins for both low and high capacity products. In addition, low capacity utilisation in the first half 1997 had led to reduced income for the division.
"In the short term we have taken actions to reduce costs in all activities not directly related to product development and marketing in order to improve profitability," Birkeland said.
"Phasing of a new product generation, starting this autumn, will significantly improve the competitive edge of the business area from 1998."
First-half new orders for the satellite communications business rose 164 million crowns to 570 million crowns, mainly due to a rise in orders for the WorldPhone, Nera said.
The company had delivered 5,000 WorldPhones as of June 30 and had increased production speed threefold compared with the beginning of the year.

Nera plans to deliver 15,000 to 20,000 telephones during 1997 and will launch the marine version of the WorldPhone in September, making high-quality satellite communications available to yachts, coastal vessels and fishing boats.
